notes: Assessment 1 dates conflict: the brief gives 16 November 2026 and feedback 7 December; the handbook and introduction slides give 11 November and feedback 2 December. Confirm with the module lead. No submission time is provided. Assessment 2 remains 6 January 2027, with feedback 27 January.
Use Harvard referencing throughout your work.
Both assessments are AIAS Level 2: AI planning. Include the required declaration and follow the individual assessment brief.
The handbook lists one four-hour session per week for 12 weeks and 150 hours of independent study. Check your personal timetable for teaching times.
Teaching combines lectures and practical workshops. The indicative sequence covers entity relationships, logical modelling, the relational model, normalisation and RDBMS architecture.

Arrange a meeting with the module lead between 26 and 30 October 2026 to review your draft logical data model (LDM). Contact the module lead when you have a viable draft. The meeting time must be arranged individually.
Groups of 5-6 students are to be assigned by Week 3. You can begin reviewing requirements before your group is allocated.
Complete all six SQL workbooks before starting Assessment 2. Assessment 2 requires a personal reflection on how the workbooks supported your implementation.

Each assessment requires an individual peer review/reflection form as well as the group submission. Missing the individual form counts as non-submission for that student. Confirm the Assessment 1 deadline because the sources disagree.

Assessment 1 practises requirements analysis, an annotated logical data model and evidence of normalisation to at least 3NF, with a report evaluating the design against client needs. Rubric: requirements 20%, modelling 30%, approach 25%, evaluation 15%, presentation 10%.
Assessment 2 assesses implementation scripts, data/report queries, planning, testing and evaluation. Rubric: database creation 25%, user reports 20%, planning 20%, testing 15%, evaluation 20%.

Brief wording needs clarification: the cover tables refer to individual reports (and website files in Assessment 2), while the main instructions describe group database work. Follow the module team's clarification. Assessment 1 also describes the review meeting as weeks beginning 26 and 30 October; the introduction slides say between those dates. Confirm the appointment window.
